subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should ordinary `message.send` hide or strip poll creation fields, or should OpenClaw keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields such as `pollQuestion` and `pollOption` on send?
rationale: Current main intentionally fixed metadata-only false positives but still rejects content-bearing poll fields, and changing that behavior affects the shared model-facing message-tool contract across channels.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for `poll` or channel-specific poll-capable surfaces so plain sends cannot inherit them from the shared schema.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and remove poll creation fields before delivery, improving send reliability while possibly masking mistaken poll calls.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Preserve the shipped content-bearing rejection and require stronger live evidence before changing the shared message-tool contract.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for `poll` or channel-specific poll-capable surfaces so plain sends cannot inherit them from the shared schema.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll gating and schema consistency work is the strongest current history signal for the shared send/poll boundary.
